Ruby's `Regexp.escape` is a core-library call with no JS counterpart; each port spells the same escaping through a file-local helper (`regexpEscape`, `escapeRegExp`) or an inline character-class replace, so the call is made under a different name. Pre-existing divergence, newly VISIBLE to the gate: `escape` only entered the ported-call population when `ActiveSupport::FileUpdateChecker#escape` (file_update_checker.rb:146-148) was ported.

`Regexp.new(patterns.join("|"))` (parameter_filter.rb:64-65) — a Ruby Regexp is Unicode-aware with no flag to say so, while a JS Regexp only reads `\p{...}` as a property escape under an explicit `u`/`v` flag. The port's second argument spells the property Ruby's constructor has implicitly, so the joined group Regexp keeps the semantics of the members it folds in; there is no one-argument JS spelling of it.
